target_customer: General contractors and construction owners paying for daily jobsite capture and analytics
problem: Tracking construction progress, safety and quality by hand is slow and inconsistent.
business_model: Robot as a service for jobsites, booked per project
product_category: Construction robotics and AI site monitoring

founders.name: Lana Graf
education: MIT (a job post says the company was founded by MIT alumni)

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous navigation of messy, changing construction sites plus robot hardware and AI analysis is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus accumulated site imagery and builder partnerships raise barriers, though several construction capture vendors exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying or purchase was found.

market_need_then: Gilbane partnered with Nextera on the Didge platform for jobsite capture, reported by Construction Dive, and Skanska was reported deploying two robots on a Seattle tower, indicating contractor demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Marketing quotes such as these robots never take a day off, from customer testimonials.

branding.brand_signature: The Didge product name, used with Gilbane as a co-branded platform.
branding.community_and_virality: Co-branded launch coverage with Gilbane in construction trade press.

brand_strength.rationale: Product name Didge gained trade coverage via Gilbane, but the company carries two names (Nextera and Didge) which splits recognition.

outcome_analysis: Nextera Robotics is an MIT founded company that joined YC Summer 2020 and settled on construction site robots under the Didge product, with a Gilbane partnership and Skanska deployments reported. It has about 20 staff and is still active, but funding is only vaguely reported by aggregators, so how well it has done financially is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights shows 500K USD in a convertible note dated January 2020, Caplight shows 350K USD in December 2020, Seedtable roughly 500K with YC and Seabed VC (estimated split); aggregators only, so none recorded. Founded year conflicts (YC says 2015, CB Insights says 2020). The YC tags mention autonomous delivery, but later sources show a construction focus, which may be a pivot not dated in sources. Competitor search returned only undated or later material (Starship, Nuro, Kiwibot, Dusty Robotics), so the list is empty. The Skanska deployment comes from an aggregator summary.
